title: Emrys and the Summer
premise: Ansel Ishikawa, a lighthouse keeper's grandson and part-time novelist, has spent a decade rehearsing one sentence he's never dared say to Emrys Vale, his late grandfather's ward and now the reluctant heir to the failing Vale vineyard. When a freak June snowstorm strands Ansel, Emrys, and Emrys's polished fiancé-to-be at the isolated keeper's cottage, old rivalries and older feelings thaw all at once. As the vineyard's first harvest approaches under threat of sale to a resort developer, Ansel must finally speak the rehearsed sentence — choosing love against duty — before Emrys signs away both the land and them.
about_author: Petra Villalobos is a former sommelier who writes love stories set wherever weather misbehaves. She lives above an old orchard with her partner and a dog named after a grape she can no longer afford.

chapters.title: The Muscle of the Heart
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ten years after leaving the coast, novelist Ansel returns to the lighthouse cottage to finish a book, insisting to himself that hearts are trainable muscles. He learns Emrys Vale has inherited the neighboring vineyard. Beat: guarded nostalgia masking dread.

chapters.title: Ward of the Vale
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys arrives to survey the vineyard he never wanted, bound by his adoptive father's will to run one harvest before selling. He discovers Ansel next door and their decade-old rivalry reignites over a broken fence line. Beat: resentment sharpened by unwanted recognition.

chapters.title: First Frost in June
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A freak cold snap threatens the vines; Ansel, despite himself, shows up with frost candles from his grandfather's stores. Working side by side until dawn, they fall into old rhythms. Beat: grudging cooperation becoming dangerous comfort.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At a town tasting, Emrys introduces Julian, his investor-fiancé, as the man who will save the estate. Watching Ansel congratulate them with perfect composure, Emrys feels something crack. Beat: public performance versus private grief.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The forecast turns apocalyptic; roads close. Julian arrives early for contract signing just as the snow begins. All three are trapped at the cottage when the power fails. Beat: claustrophobic setup, forced proximity.

chapters.title: Three at the Table
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Candlelit dinner becomes a duel; Julian charms, Ansel provokes, Emrys referees badly. Old stories surface — including the night ten years ago that ended their friendship. Beat: history weaponized, wounds reopened.

chapters.title: What the Snow Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Snowbound day two: Julian works the phone signal on the ridge while Ansel and Emrys are stuck indoors together. A spilled box reveals Ansel's unpublished manuscript about two boys and a lighthouse. Beat: exposure without confession.

chapters.title: Julian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Julian privately shows Emrys the sale terms — and a clause binding Emrys personally to the resort project. Duty wears a wedding ring. Emrys signs nothing but says nothing either. Beat: the trap tightening.

chapters.title: The Cellar
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sent to fetch wine against the cold, Ansel and Emrys discover his grandfather's hidden reserve bottles labeled for 'E & A — when ready.' They drink one. Almost-kiss interrupted by Julian's shout. Beat: longing at full flood, denied.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The storm peaks; the ridge road washes out, stranding them indefinitely. Julian's frustration curdles into contempt for the 'sentimental' property. Emrys defends the vineyard before he realizes he means it. Beat: loyalty shifting ground.

chapters.title: Confessions by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Power still out, Emrys admits he read the manuscript years ago — it's why he left. Ansel learns his book caused the rupture, not healed it. Betrayal and tenderness collide. Beat: devastating midpoint reversal.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Storm breaks; roads reopen. Julian pushes to leave immediately and finalize the sale in the city. Emrys asks for one week — through first harvest. Julian gives him three days. Beat: clock started, stakes doubled.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel organizes the town to bring in the grapes early before frost returns. Emrys works beside him, learning the land his father loved. Found family forms around them — neighbors, the old foreman, Ansel's grandmother. Beat: communal warmth, belonging.

chapters.title: The Foreman's Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Old foreman Marisol reveals Emrys's father kept ledgers proving the vineyard profitable — and a letter naming Ansel's grandfather as his dearest friend. The rivalry between their families was always a fiction of pride. Beat: inherited grief reframed.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Julian returns with lawyers and a moving truck of ambition. He offers Ansel money to disappear from the narrative. Ansel refuses — then realizes refusing isn't the same as speaking. Beat: cowardice confronted.

chapters.title: Crush
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. First press of the harvest happens amid the sale chaos. Emrys tastes the year's first wine and understands what his father meant by 'when ready.' He sends Julian ahead alone. Beat: decision made in the body before the mind.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On the lighthouse gallery at dusk, Ansel finally speaks the sentence rehearsed for a decade: 'I have loved you since the summer we were seventeen.' Emrys answers not with words but by staying. Beat: climax — love declared against every duty.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Julian returns for his answer; Emrys declines the sale and the engagement, absorbing the financial ruin that may follow. Julian leaves with a flicker of respect. Beat: cost counted, chosen freely.

chapters.title: What the Town Knew
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The community rallies with an offer: a cooperative buyout preserving the vineyard, seeded by pre-orders of the first vintage. Found family becomes literal structure. Beat: private love made publicly sustainable.

chapters.title: Label: E & A
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They bottle the reserve under the old label. Emrys reads his father's final letter aloud in the cellar — a blessing written for exactly this. Beat: inheritance redefined as permission.

chapters.title: The Second Draft
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel finishes the novel, changing the ending to match the truth. Reading it aloud to Emrys in the cottage where they were stranded, he finds the storm gave more than it took. Beat: art reconciled with life.

chapters.title: Summer, Keeping
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. One year later: first harvest festival, the lighthouse lit again, two names on the vineyard deed. Ansel trains his heart no longer to contain but to open. Beat: resolution — love as the duty gladly kept.
